title: Refinement counits and their specified condensed transposes
statement: Fix a prime l and a field k of positive prime characteristic different from l. Let X,Y be separated finite-type quasi-compact k-schemes, f:X to Y a k-morphism, and c a compactification. All coefficient fields are the canonical universe lift of Q_l and its fixed algebraic closure. Let d be a second compactification, r:c to d a refinement, and C one specified coherent ComparisonFamily. Choose Contexts Pc,Pd with reduction calculi identified with C, admissible data v,w in these contexts, their AtCompactification comparison records qc,qd for exactly the corresponding specifiedSupport members of C, and an input isomorphism b:v.L to w.L. Then there is an isomorphism a between the actual ringed-sequence presentations of the two supplied systems. Its sequence counit square commutes using systemRefinement, the leftAdjointUniq comparison between the two reduction adjunctions, and b. Moreover the specified comparison iso at c followed by exceptionalRefinement and the d-right-adjoint image of U(b) equals U of the actual total-limit map of a followed by the specified comparison iso at d. All maps are the actual definitions of [def-pur-condensed-exceptional-reconstruction-data]. This asserts only compactification refinement of comparisons already supplied as AtCompactification records; it constructs neither those Conclusions nor their invertibility, system recognition, naturality for general maps, or any coefficient/shift properties.

proof.text: Use theta in qc and qd to conjugate the Brown refinement mate, including b, to the supplied systems. The intrinsic ringed proper/open refinement and its normalized support comparison preserve the Brown counits, and the mate is invertible on the bounded etale-origin systems.

Transport the normalized-coordinate refinement counit square through the supplied presentation equivalences. Their section, representative and localization mate equations fix all comparison directions. Uniqueness of the left adjoint to the same actual limit identifies the reduction comparison with the displayed leftAdjointUniq, producing the first equality.

Apply actual total limit and the reconstruction units. Coefficient-model unit/counit naturality gives the integral trace square. Rational realization and closure scalar extension carry it to the raw condensed square. The single supplied ComparisonFamily provides coherence of the two support comparisons and fixes the relative normalization. Projection mate pasting identifies its left arrow with condensedRefinement.

Transpose the raw condensed square under the exact chosen upstream adjunctions. Apply inverse homEquiv on compactification d. Its left and right naturality, the equation conjugateEquiv_counit and refinement naturality reduce the two transposes to the raw counit square. Injectivity gives the displayed right-adjoint equation.

lean.statement:
theorem condensed_exceptional_refinement_counits
    (C : CompactSupportCondensedRealization.ComparisonFamily l k)
    (X Y : Base k) (f : X.scheme ⟶ Y.scheme) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of k))]
    (c d : Compactification f) (r : c.Refinement d)
    (Pc : Context l k X Y f c) (Pd : Context l k X Y f d)
    (hc : Pc.reduction = (C.coefficient (Field.{u} l)).reduction)
    (hd : Pd.reduction = (C.coefficient (Field.{u} l)).reduction)
    (qc : AtCompactification l k (C.coefficient (Field.{u} l)).realization Pc
      (specifiedSupport l k C Pc hc))
    (qd : AtCompactification l k (C.coefficient (Field.{u} l)).realization Pd
      (specifiedSupport l k C Pd hd))
    (v : Datum l k Pc) (w : Datum l k Pd)
    (hv : v.Admissible l k) (hw : w.Admissible l k) (b : v.L ≅ w.L) :
    RefinementCompatibility l k (C.coefficient (Field.{u} l)).realization X Y f c d r
      Pc Pd (specifiedSupport l k C Pc hc) (specifiedSupport l k C Pd hd)
      qc qd v w hv hw b
